Sienno Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Stara Wieś, Poland

Demolished. Jewish settlement in Sienno dates to the 16th century, though the community grew significantly only after 1650. By 1921, 735 Jews made up nearly 44% of the population; most were murdered at Treblinka in late 1942. The cemetery's founding date is unclear, though it likely predates 1837, and it was enlarged in 1869. During the German occupation, the site doubled as an execution ground - in autumn 1942, military police shot a man named Nojech there. Poland formally closed the cemetery in 1964, by which point nearly all above-ground traces had vanished; the area served as pasture into the 1980s. A symbolic brick gate went up in 1982, later joined by a bilingual Hebrew-Polish memorial plaque and several recovered sandstone stelae.
